decks.notes: The main strategy of this deck is to quickly assemble the Time Vault and Voltaic Key combo, which allows the player to take infinite turns. The deck also utilizes mana acceleration from various Mox cards and artifacts like Mana Vault and Grim Monolith to power out the combo pieces quickly. Additionally, the deck includes powerful disruptive cards like Force of Will and Tinker to protect the combo and disrupt the opponent's game plan. The Coveted Jewel serves as both a win condition and a way to generate additional mana to further enable the combo. The deck aims to win the game quickly and decisively through its powerful combo and disruptive elements.

The key concept of this Dimir Control deck is to disrupt the opponent's resources while efficiently drawing cards and controlling the game. By using powerful cards like Ancestral Recall, Force of Will, and Narset, Parter of Veils, the deck aims to control the tempo of the game and prevent the opponent from executing their game plan. The deck also includes powerful mana acceleration with cards like Sol Ring and Black Lotus to power out threats like Bolas's Citadel or Time Vault. The deck's win condition is to outvalue and outmaneuver the opponent through efficient control and card advantage.

The main focus of this deck is to control the game by utilizing powerful cards and spells to disrupt the opponent's strategy, while also generating card advantage and controlling the board. The deck includes a mix of efficient counterspells, card draw, and removal, along with powerful win conditions like Karn, the Great Creator and Teferi, Time Raveler. Additionally, the deck includes powerful tutors like Demonic Tutor and Vampiric Tutor to help find key cards quickly, as well as combos like Time Vault and Voltaic Key or Tinker to quickly close out games.

The focus of this deck is to control the game by using powerful Planeswalker cards like Dack Fayden, Narset, Parter of Veils, and Oko, Thief of Crowns. The deck also includes disruptive spells like Force of Will and Flusterstorm to ensure control over the game. Additionally, the deck features efficient removal in the form of cards like Baleful Strix and Wrenn and Six, while also having access to powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time. Overall, this deck aims to dominate the game through careful planning and strategic control of the battlefield.

The main concept of this Dimir Control deck is to disrupt the opponent's game plan with various counterspells and disruptive creatures such as Hullbreacher and Opposition Agent, while also using powerful card draw and tutor effects to find key combo pieces like Time Vault and Bolas's Citadel. The deck aims to control the game through efficient card advantage and resource denial, ultimately outvaluing the opponent and securing a win through its powerful win conditions. The inclusion of strong vintage staples like Ancestral Recall and Black Lotus further enhances the deck's strategy of controlling the game.

The main strategy revolves around assembling the necessary cards to cast Doomsday, followed by casting Thassa's Oracle to win the game. The deck includes a variety of tutors, card draw spells, and countermagic to help find and protect the combo pieces. The use of fast mana in the form of Moxen and rituals allows for explosive plays and quick wins. The deck is designed to be streamlined and efficient, focusing on quickly setting up the combo while disrupting the opponent's game plan.

The key strategy of this Grixis Control deck is to disrupt the opponent's game plan while assembling powerful combos and card advantage engines. The deck utilizes a variety of powerful spells such as Demonic Tutor, Ancestral Recall, and Tinker to find key threats like Sphinx of the Steel Wind and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse. It also includes disruptive cards like Narset, Parter of Veils and Opposition Agent to control the opponent's resources. The deck aims to dominate the board through efficient removal spells and counterspells while also generating mana advantage through cards like Sol Ring and Moxen.

This deck aims to disrupt the opponent's strategy by playing hatebears such as Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and Spirit of the Labyrinth while applying pressure with aggressive creatures like Anointed Peacekeeper and Archon of Emeria. The deck also utilizes disruptive artifacts like Chalice of the Void and Trinisphere to slow down the opponent's game plan. With access to powerful lands like Karakas and Wasteland, as well as mana acceleration from Ancient Tomb and Chrome Mox, the deck aims to establish an early board presence and control the game through disruptive creatures and spells.
